Hi Maya / Tim —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we committed to follow up on:

- Your top-level goals: low-latency authoring for in-product fraud alerts and a streaming UX for investigator notes. You called out p95 latency and predictable concurrency as deal breakers.
- Clarify expected steady-state concurrency, burst profile, and streaming chunking cadence so we can size connection pooling and quota ceilings.
- Redwood action items: draft a pragmatic concurrency quota we can pilot with, recommended connection multiplexing settings, and a short SLA draft to put on the table.

Could you confirm the acceptance criteria below (so we can finalize the pilot proposal):
1) Sustained parallel active requests: ~1.2k (does that match your telemetry?),
2) Burst tolerance: up to 3k parallel requests for ~30s,
3) p95 generation latency target (non-streaming): <= 800 ms for median prompts (~50 tokens),
4) Streaming requirements: initial token within 200ms, subsequent chunks every ~150–250ms, and per-stream idle cutoff of 30s,
5) Connection model: prefer persistent sockets from app => Redwood (multiplexed), with session affinity for KV + prefix caching.

If those are roughly right, we’ll send a short rate proposal and a pilot SLA to sign.

Thanks —

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap. Pretty close. A few clarifications from our side (we pulled numbers from our infra team):

- Steady-state concurrency: 1,000 active requests during business hours (we can provision more off-peak),
- Burst profile: spikes to ~2,800 concurrent requests for up to 45 seconds during settlement windows,
- Throughput: average ~3,500 requests/minute, peak ~12k requests/minute during rush,
- Latency: p95 <= 1s is acceptable for non-streaming; streaming initial frame < 250ms and subsequent frames every 200ms is what our UX needs,
- Multiplexing: we prefer a small number of long-lived sockets from each region (3–6 sockets per pod) with per-socket multiplexing; we cannot open tens of thousands of TCP connections from our service.

Two additional asks:
- What does throttling look like? We need a clear fallback story for degraded capacity (drop to cached responses or lower-fidelity model), and
- Cost/credit flexibility for the pilot window (30 days).

If you can send a concrete quota + fallback matrix and one-pager SLA we’ll route to procurement.

—Maya

Hi Maya / Tim —

Appreciate the detail — below is a pragmatic pilot proposal that balances predictability for you and safe operating limits for Redwood. I’ve included the two short artifacts as attachments: a connection/concurrency matrix and a one-page pilot SLA.

Proposal (pilot, 30 days):
- Pilot quota (soft): 1,500 parallel active requests (global), enforced via per-api-key connection counters.
- Burst allowance (elastic): up to 3,200 parallel requests for burst windows; sustained bursts >60s will trigger scaled backoff policies.
- Throughput alignment: nominal allowance 10k req/min across the account with per-key burst tokens (10k token bucket).
- Streaming SLOs: initial token emitted <= 225ms (measured from request accept), subsequent frames target 200ms cadence; we’ll instrument chunk frequency and report weekly.
- Connection model: recommend 4 persistent sockets per regional pod (recommended starting point). Each socket will multiplex up to ~375 concurrent logical streams (we internally shard routing by session id to keep KV cache affinity).
- Backpressure / throttling: when pilot quota is exceeded we offer a graded fallback matrix: 1) short 429 with Retry-After for small bursts, 2) route to cached (prefix) responses for predictable prompts, 3) fall back to a smaller, faster quantized model for non-critical UX. We will provide a header X-Redwood-Fallback indicating which path was taken.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Connection multiplexing reduces TCP footprint but increases per-socket CPU on our side; the 4-socket-per-pod starting point is chosen to keep socket counts low while maintaining KV affinity.
- If you expect many independent client pods, we suggest a small connection broker per region to limit ephemeral socket explosion.
- We can instrument per-route p95 and an endpoint-level concurrency gauge so Skyline (your SRE) can see live headroom.

Costs / credits for pilot:
- Estimated incremental cost for pilot at the proposed pilot quota: ~$8k–11k/month (blended across token and reserved capacity),
- Redwood will apply a one-time pilot credit of $6k for the 30-day trial to offset initial ramp.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the pilot quota and burst ceiling,
2) We’ll share the SLA draft (attached) + a DocuSign link for signature,
3) Redwood infra team will provision the pilot keys and a short-run playbook for traffic shaping and failover.

Attachments included: 2026-10-16_stellarpay_conn_matrix.xlsx, 2026-10-16_SLA-draft-v1.pdf
